text: {{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Cathayan general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. Behind the general, Jade Warriors are already forming ranks with halberds levelled. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Kislevite general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. Behind the general, boyars wrapped in bear furs are already drawing their men into line. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}An Ogre general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. Behind the general, his warriors slap their gut-plates and drool at the thought of the feast to come. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Nurglite general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. Behind the general, his rotting ranks are already shambling into line under a cloud of buzzing flies. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A Tzeentchian general blocks our path and calls out a challenge, a skirmish to settle which army is the stronger. Behind the general, his soldiers are forming ranks under shifting, many-coloured banners. He says he sees many battles in our future. Do we accept?
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Their leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the Dragon for his love. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Their leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking Ursun for his love. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Their leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the Maw for its blessings. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}On the road we come across a battered camp full of ragged, hostile malcontents. Their leader gives us a mocking salute, thanking the gods of Chaos for their power. The rest raise their weapons, some with shaking hands, ready to attack. What should we do?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A faint smell of gunpowder drifts across the empty road, and the soldiers feel they are being watched. As the vanguard advances, a birdcall sounds from the hedges, and another answers it. Should we continue down this path?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The army pushes through a thick, damp forest where little light reaches the ground. Every snapping twig sounds like a footstep, and the trees seem to shift when no one is looking. The vanguard reports voices among the branches and advises us to prepare for an ambush. Should we continue down this path?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Hoofbeats and howling circle the long line of the army on every side. Crazed screams and curses in a crude, guttural tongue ring out, but no one shows themselves. They seem to be followers of the Dark Gods, and they want a toll before they let us through. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The cackle of hobgoblins fills the night air, coming from every shadow around us. We see the slavers circling our encampment, testing whether it can be easily assaulted. They seem sloppy and overconfident. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores. Corpses riddled with arrows lie everywhere. Some survivors, deliberately left alive, tell our general it was "for the good of all". The invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores. Half-eaten corpses and trampled houses are everywhere. Some survivors, deliberately left alive, babble to our general about "giant lizards" and lizardmen. The invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large band of invaders in the distance. They are pushing into lands we claim, looting small towns and carting off their stores. No corpses are seen anywhere. Most of the towns seem abandoned, with traces of sea water where there should be none. The use of magic here is clearly felt. The invaders mean to settle this land, or strip it bare if they cannot hold it.
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The forest glows under the light of Morrslieb as the army passes through. The night is full of sounds that should not be there, and guttural grunts carry from the edges of the column. A huge beast crashes into the outer column before our soldiers drive it back. They look to their general for orders. What should we do?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The road winds through a pass between the mountains. Small caves surround the path and the silence is heavy. The outer columns warn of red eyes in the dark, and the chattering is too loud to come from ordinary rats. The soldiers of the vanguard advise attacking the caves before they attack us! What should we do?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A great greenskin horde gathers on the hilltop, beating crude drums and bellowing insults down the slope. They are waiting for our column to halt so they can charge. Shall we try our luck?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A large army of dark elf slavers has made camp in a remote corner of this province, empty cages stacked on its wagons. They clearly mean to raid our settlements for slaves. The rough ground has hidden our approach, and they have not seen us yet. Should we try to intercept them?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Locals tell of a necromancer hiding in a remote graveyard, where the earth is turned over fresh every night. He is raising an army to march on our lands, and it grows with every grave he empties. Should we attack him before he gets out of control?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Under the green light of Morrslieb, our advance party sees a strange sight. Skeletons in gold and fine linen, marching beside great constructs that move as if alive, are chasing a long band of Norscan marauders. When they spot us, a large contingent breaks off and turns our way, ready in case we think of interfering.
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A huge band of Slayers stands before us, crests of orange hair bristling, and Gotrek and Felix march at its head. They seem to have been sent to destroy us, and they keep chasing us on their short legs no matter how much ground we put between us. Why are we in the dwarfs' Book of Grudges?
An Epic Battle!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}"SKARBRAND HATES YOU!" the Bloodthirster bellows. The ground shakes as he strides closer, his axes dragging furrows through the earth. "YOUR SKULL BELONGS AT THE FOOT OF THE THRONE! PREPARE TO DIE!" The gaze of the Blood God falls on us, and the ranks grip their weapons tighter. No one here means to run from him.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Khorne's consort towers over us like a fallen angel, wings spread wide. "Khorne calls you to serve his glory! I will be the one to test you! I will be the one to decide if you are worthy to worship our lord! Die and let me decorate his throne with your skull!" The Blood God is watching. Our warriors hold their ground, eager to prove they are worth his notice.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our lord dreams of a fiery-eyed warrior who points the way to a hidden clearing near the camp. On waking, a strange fury takes hold, and the army marches to the place from the dream. A greater daemon and its warband are there, and they did not expect us. "Who dares defy the will of the Blood God? Prepare to die." The daemonic army readies to attack. The fury from the dream has not faded. The army wants this fight, and the Blood God is watching.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A huge, swift daemon approaches, and we know him from the stories. Azazel looks at us almost fondly. "Little one, there is something strange about this sword. I think the Dark Prince blessed it once, but now it reeks of blood and rage, and it makes the dead come after me. Don't get me wrong, it's a lot of fun. But if we fight here, I think I can be rid of it. What do you say? It's a fun idea, isn't it?" He waits, hopeful. The blade has gone over to the Blood God, and so has the warband around it. Somewhere beyond the veil, the Blood God is watching. Our warriors are hungry for this fight.
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}We come upon a lavish, openly debauched camp that looks more like a carnival than a war camp. Its general is Sigvald the Magnificent, beautiful as a painted saint, and he looks us over with open disgust. "My god sometimes surprises me when he presents me with horrible, unpresentable things like you." He waves a scornful hand but keeps talking. "He sent me to give you a gift so that you would consider joining us. But seeing you here, so pathetic and weak, I have decided to keep it. You are clearly undeserving of his favour." The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. Our greed will not let him keep what was meant for us. Embrace the temptation!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A strange, magnificent castle stands where none stood before, plainly a work of Chaos, and we feel compelled to enter. Wine runs from the fountains and the halls ring with revelry. N'Kari, the Keeper of Secrets, welcomes us. "Nice to have you here. Do you feel her gaze? She makes me feel... wild. She wants to see you and me fight. I promise if you win I'll make it count for you." The daemon licks his lips with a long, lascivious tongue. "And if you lose, well, we'll still have fun... as much as possible." He laughs. The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. The hunger in our heart urges us to take his challenge. Embrace the temptation!
A Gift From Chaos

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Deep in the night our lookouts start screaming, and some of them die before the camp is roused. An emissary walks out of the dark, a stunningly beautiful dark elf. "The Dark Prince wants me to present you with a gift. It seems that he has chosen you as his protégé. But I can always get a better deal if I kidnap you instead of giving you his gift." She weighs us with a calculating gaze. "I'll give you a chance to disappear. He's never liked cowards, so if he sees you running away I can just take his gift. Make a decision or die." The Dark Prince's gaze rests on us, sweet as poison. Our greed will not let her walk off with what is ours. Embrace the temptation!

This smithy is held by [[col:red]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]], and its master has hired blades to guard the forge. We can storm it and take it for ourselves, opening its forge to our generals and heroes, though a grander forge keeps tougher guards.\\n\\nWin the battle and the smithy is ours. Lose, and it stays under their control.\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_relations").StringValue}}
Seizing the Smithy

An enemy army marches on the smithy. The blacksmiths take up weapons from their own racks, and the guard detachment forms up at the forge door. If we do not stand with them, the smithy falls into enemy hands.
Defending the Smithy

The master blacksmith looks at us anxiously and asks us to choose one of his works. The quality is clearly poor, but it will still serve our army. Or we could give him the gold to expand the smithy, so that it pays its taxes faster and turns out better equipment on our next visit.\\n
The Master Blacksmith's Offer

The master blacksmith looks at us seriously and asks us to choose one of his works. The quality is clearly good, and it will serve our army well. Or we could give him the gold to expand the smithy, so that it pays its taxes faster and turns out better equipment on our next visit.\\n
The Master Blacksmith's Trust
The master blacksmith smiles and asks us to choose one of his masterpieces. The quality is clearly excellent, and it will serve our army well.
The Master Blacksmith's Gift
A Test of Arms

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A rival general blocks the road with a modest force and calls out a challenge. They want to see whether our army is worth fearing. Do we accept?
Nascent Rebellion

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}We come across a battered camp full of armed malcontents who clearly do not welcome our presence. Their leaders shout for blood, and the mob raises its weapons. What should we do?
Bandits!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The road ahead is too quiet. Fresh hoofprints cross it in every direction, and the scouts swear riders are shadowing the column from the tree line. Should we continue down this path?
Possible Ambush?

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The column stretches thin through broken ground. Too many birds take flight at once, and the rearguard reports shapes moving along the ridges. The soldiers look to their general. What should we do?
Raid!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Our advance party reports a large foreign force in the distance, looting small towns and carting off everything of value. The survivors say the invaders mean to take this land or strip it bare. What should we do?
An Epic Battle!

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A great army waits in battle lines on the far side of the field, banners raised and war drums pounding. Its general has chosen this ground and expects us to answer. Shall we try our luck?
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith shows us what the forge has on hand. We may take one piece freely while the forge is ready, commission a masterwork for gold, or pay to improve the forge so its work grows finer.
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith wipes the soot from his hands: "Not much on the racks yet, but every piece is honest work."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 1 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]common or uncommon[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]] longer than the Smithy cooldown after a free piece (10 turns by default)\\n- Commission: one rare masterwork for [[col:yellow]]5000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]15 turns[[/col]]\\n- Improve to level 2: [[col:yellow]]10000[[/col]] gold
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith nods towards the racks: "Good steel, all of it. The Association stamped every piece itself."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 2 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]uncommon or rare[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: [[col:yellow]]2 turns[[/col]] longer than the Smithy cooldown after a free piece (7 turns by default)\\n- Commission: one rare masterwork for [[col:yellow]]10000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]10 turns[[/col]]\\n- Improve to level 3: [[col:yellow]]20000[[/col]] gold
The Master Blacksmith's Forge

The master blacksmith spreads his arms over the racks: "The finest work in the Association. Take your pick."\\n\\nThis forge belongs to the [[col:yellow]]Smiths' Association[[/col]], which honours its patrons at every smithy.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Forge level 3 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Free pieces: [[col:yellow]]rare[[/col]], one per visit\\n- Ready again: after the [[col:yellow]]Smithy cooldown[[/col]] once a free piece is taken (5 turns by default)\\n- Commission: two rare masterworks for [[col:yellow]]15000[[/col]] gold\\n- Tribute: one item every [[col:yellow]]5 turns[[/col]]\\n- Unique commission: one unique piece for [[col:yellow]]20000[[/col]] gold
The Ancient Tower

An ancient tower rises before us, its gates held by a hostile warband. Five floors lead up to the Master of the Tower, and every floor we take adds to the haul.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Floors[[/col]]\\n- Floor 1: easy\\n- Floors 2 to 4: medium\\n- Floor 5: the Master of the Tower, hard\\n\\nAfter each victory we may climb higher or leave with the haul. Our losses carry over from floor to floor. [[col:red]]Losing any floor forfeits the whole haul.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Between floors[[/col]]\\nAfter each victory the tower offers deals for the climb ahead: healing, buffs, sabotage, gambles and more. [[col:yellow]]Missions[[/col]] set a goal for the next battle and pay only if we fight that battle ourselves. [[col:red]]An auto-resolved battle does not count.[[/col]]
The Master Has Fallen

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_result_floor_5").StringValue}}The Master of the Tower lies dead at our feet, and every floor is ours. Its vaults stand open.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The climb[[/col]]\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_climb_floor_5").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The whole haul is ours to claim.[[/col]]
Tower Floor 1 Cleared

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_result_floor_1").StringValue}}The floor is ours, and the way up lies open. Our army has had no time to recover.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]The climb[[/col]]\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tower_climb_floor_1").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Floor 2 adds to the haul[[/col]]\\n- 2000 gold, up to 3000 for a clean win\\n- 2 uncommon or rare items\\n\\nClimb higher for a richer haul, or leave now and keep what we have. [[col:red]]Losing the next floor forfeits the whole haul.[[/col]]\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Missions[[/col]] set a goal for the next battle and pay only if we fight that battle ourselves. [[col:red]]An auto-resolved battle does not count.[[/col]]
An Ally Beset

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}Smoke rises beyond the next ridge, where an allied army stands surrounded. Their lines are bending, and the enemy brought far more warriors than it needs. If we march now, we can fight at their side and turn the day. Win, and their kin across these lands will remember who came to help.
Turn the Tables

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}The scouts of our allied escort come back at a run. An enemy war party lies hidden along the road ahead, waiting for us to walk into its trap, and it does not know it has been seen. If we strike first, together, we can catch it in the open. Win, and the escort's kin will hear of it.
Relief Column

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_spot_battle_missions").StringValue}}A messenger reaches us half dead. An allied army is cut off, and the enemy is closing in for the kill. They will not hold for long. If we march hard, we can reach them before their line breaks, and some of those we save may choose to fight under our banner.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 1 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 2 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
The Tavern

{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_scene").StringValue}}\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_tavern_greeting").StringValue}}\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Tavern level 3 of 3[[/col]]\\n- Run by the Tavern Keepers' Guild: hold 1 of its contracts at a time, from any of its Taverns.\\n- Owned by [[col:yellow]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]]. Only the owner can improve it.
Seizing the Tavern

This tavern is held by [[col:red]]{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_owner").StringValue}}[[/col]], and its keeper has hired blades to guard the premises. We can storm it and take it for ourselves, though a grander tavern keeps tougher guards.\\n\\nWin the battle and the tavern is ours. Lose, and it stays in their hands.\\n\\n{{CcoCampaignEventDilemma:ScriptObjectContext("land_enc_point_relations").StringValue}}
Defending the Tavern
An enemy army marches on the tavern. The keeper bars the door, and the guards he hired form up in the yard with their weapons drawn. If we do not stand with them, the tavern falls into enemy hands.
The Mercenary Hall

Sellswords of every stripe drink and dice in the back hall, waiting for a lord with gold. The companies here are for hire to every visitor, for a price, and new ones arrive every 5 turns.\\n\\nThe broker looks up from his ledger: "Gold first, then take your pick. Two companies at most. I can't have you emptying the place."\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: 3 companies of tier 1 or 2, and 1 of our own kind.\\n- Level 2: 4 companies up to tier 3, 1 famous regiment, 1 of our own kind and a rank 5 hero.\\n- Level 3: 5 companies up to tier 4, 1 or 2 famous regiments, 2 of our own kind and a rank 10 hero.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Hire up to 2, after which the hall will not deal with us for 5 turns, or go back to the common room.[[/col]]
The Contract Board

Notices crowd the board by the door, each stamped with the seal of the Tavern Keepers' Guild: bounties on lords who have made enemies of the Guild, and purses for anyone who will thin out a foe troubling its roads. Each contract asks a deposit, returned with the reward when the work is done. Fail one or drop it, and the deposit is lost. Every Tavern of the Guild then charges us a quarter more for 10 turns.\\n\\nA Guild clerk taps the board with an inky finger: "Read them carefully. The Guild does not forget a broken contract."\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: easy contracts for a 1000 gold deposit, paying 1500 to 2000 gold and an uncommon item. Culls ask for 2 armies.\\n- Level 2: medium contracts for a 2000 gold deposit, paying 3000 to 3500 gold and a rare item. Culls ask for 3 armies.\\n- Level 3: hard contracts for a 3000 gold deposit, paying 4500 to 5000 gold and a rare item. Culls ask for 4 armies, and a three-step quest ends with a legendary item.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]We can hold 1 contract at a time, from any Tavern. Drop it from the missions panel to take another.[[/col]]
Hidden Tomb

A forgotten tomb lies half-buried in the hillside, its door split by roots and time. The wards carved into the stone are old, but not all of them have failed, and something inside still remembers how to bite.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Abandoned Camp

Cold fires and empty tents stand in a sheltered hollow. Whoever camped here left in a hurry, and left their stores and a fair share of loot behind.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Buried Relics

Bones of something enormous jut from the churned earth. Among them lie older things, weapons and charms buried long before the beast ever died here.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Hidden Temple

A temple rises from the wilds, its walls choked with vines but its altar swept clean, as if someone still tends it. Its keepers left long ago, yet offerings laid here are still answered.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Caravan Remnants

A half-sacked caravan lies across the road, its wagons overturned and its goods scattered in the mud. The raiders were in a hurry, and they missed more than they took.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
A Voice in the Dream

Our lord wakes from a dream more vivid than any waking hour. A voice spoke in it, offering strength for the trials ahead, and some of its gifts come with a price.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
The Explorers
A band of weathered explorers shares our fire for the night. They trade maps and tales of the road ahead, and ask only for safe passage in return.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Legendary Bard

A famous bard sits in chains in a bandit camp we have just put to flight. Freed, they promise to sing of our deeds in every hall and war camp across the land.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Ruined Shrine

A burnt-out shrine stands by the road, its idols blackened and cracked. Offerings left here may be answered with a blessing, or with something far less kind.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Smugglers' Cache

Crates and barrels lie hidden under a false floor, and their owners watch us from the treeline. They deal in goods and secrets, and they are open to offers.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Beast Lair
Something big lives in this cave. Fresh bones litter the entrance, and the stench carries on the wind for a mile.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Old Battlefield

Crows wheel over an old battlefield where two armies broke each other long ago. Wrecked war machines and unburied bones still lie half sunk in the mud.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Witch's Hut

A crooked hut squats in the marsh, thick with smoke and stranger smells. The witch who lives here deals in pacts and curses, and every one of them has a price.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Collapsed Mine

A collapsed mine yawns in the hillside, its lower galleries half-flooded. The deeper tunnels are still rich, and still deadly to anyone who lingers.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Merchant's Wagon
A travelling merchant has lost the road and most of their escort. Far from any market and glad of any customer, they throw open their wagon to us.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Sunken Library

A library has sunk into the marsh, its shelves rotting in black water. Some scrolls survive, sealed in wax and lead, holding the secrets of other realms.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
Spoils of War

The field is ours. Enemy dead lie in heaps, and their baggage stands abandoned where they broke and ran. Before we march on, there is more to take from this victory.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or walk away.[[/col]]
The Bar

The keeper leans on the bar beside barrels for every taste. Over at the tables, strangers are rolling dice, and a hulking champion waits for anyone brave enough to lock arms with them.\\n\\nThe barkeep turns to us: "What'll it be?"\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]By Tavern level:[[/col]]\\n- Level 1: the house brews (Fighting Spirits gives +5), a feast heals half of each unit's losses, rumours cover the 3 nearest regions, and beating the champion is worth 500 experience.\\n- Level 2: stronger brews (+10), a feast heals three quarters of the losses, rumours cover 5 regions, and the champion is worth 750 experience.\\n- Level 3: the strongest brews (+15), a feast heals every loss, rumours cover 7 regions, and the champion is worth 1000 experience.\\n\\n[[col:yellow]]Choose one, or go back to the common room.[[/col]]
